info.name: Payment Service
info.description:
One payment service for every module (ambulance, doctor appointments, lab/scan, home care), backed by Razorpay. See README.md.

SETUP
1. Import this collection and one environment: "local" (service on :8083) or "via gateway" (:8080).
2. Tokens: this service only verifies JWTs. Locally (profile "local") mint them with this repo's dev key:
     node scripts/dev-jwt.mjs patient-42 PATIENT   -> patientToken   (patientId must be the same: patient-42)
     node scripts/dev-jwt.mjs patient-99 PATIENT   -> otherPatientToken
     node scripts/dev-jwt.mjs admin-1 ADMIN        -> adminToken
   Otherwise log in through the auth service. Dev tokens last 12 h.
3. Start the service so checkouts wait for the (simulated) Razorpay webhook:
     PAYMENT_MOCK_AUTO_PAY=false ./mvnw spring-boot:run "-Dspring-boot.run.profiles=local"

RUN
Folders 1-4 run top to bottom in the Collection Runner (deselect 5 and 7 unless their variables are set). Requests marked [Simulate Razorpay] sign events with razorpayWebhookSecret exactly as Razorpay does, because Razorpay cannot reach localhost. Against real Razorpay (test mode), pay on the checkoutUrl with a test card and use "Refresh from Razorpay" instead.

AUTH
Collection default: Bearer {{patientToken}}. The refunds folder uses {{adminToken}}. Webhooks and ops use no token; folder 7 uses Basic auth with the Razorpay API key.

item.name: 1. Pay for a booking (happy path)
item.description:
The flow every module (ambulance, appointments, ...) goes through. Run in order.

Locally, start the service with PAYMENT_MOCK_AUTO_PAY=false, so the checkout stays PENDING until step 5 simulates Razorpay's webhook. With the default auto-pay, step 1 already returns PAID.

if (d.status === "PAID") console.warn("Mock auto-pay is on: restart with PAYMENT_MOCK_AUTO_PAY=false to walk through the webhook steps.");

Same Idempotency-Key: same payment and the same checkout URL. No second Razorpay payment link.
Payer or ADMIN. Anyone else gets 404.

request.description:
Stands in for Razorpay calling us (Razorpay cannot reach localhost). Signed with razorpayWebhookSecret, which must equal the service's RAZORPAY_WEBHOOK_SECRET (local profile default: local-razorpay-webhook-secret).

The service marks the payment PAID and queues the signed callback to the module (AMBULANCE_BOOKING -> ambulance service). If the ambulance service is not running, the log shows the callback being retried.
Byte-for-byte the event from step 5 (same X-Razorpay-Event-Id). Accepted with 200, applied only once.
Calling intents for a paid booking is harmless: it returns PAID, no new checkout.
The app calls this when the user returns from the checkout page, instead of waiting for Razorpay's webhook. Asks Razorpay about any open checkout and returns the current state.

5. Module side: test your module's callback endpoint
item.description:
Calls a MODULE (not this service) exactly the way the payment service does, so you can test a module's webhook handler on its own. Signed with moduleWebhookSecret, which must equal the module's PAYMENT_WEBHOOK_SECRET and this service's <MODULE>_PAYMENT_WEBHOOK_SECRET.

Header scheme: X-Payment-Timestamp = epoch seconds, X-Payment-Signature = hex(HMAC-SHA256(secret, timestamp + "." + rawBody)).

request.description: For the ambulance service, bookingId must be a booking in PAYMENT_PENDING whose fare is <= amount, or it answers 404/409. Set moduleBookingId and amount first.

item.name: 7. Razorpay direct (setup and debugging)
